app_info.subtitle: Macro financial stress data
app_info.description: LiquidityWatch provides access to E3D's macroeconomic intelligence platform through ChatGPT. Explore current financial stress conditions, Treasury and funding markets, Federal Reserve policy, energy-market developments, global liquidity, and cryptocurrency implications. Retrieve historical financial stress evaluations, examine how sub-indicators (Treasury stress, funding stress, Fed/Treasury response, AI economic impulse, energy stress, global liquidity) have changed over time, and, when available, explore the causal relationships connecting macroeconomic developments to financial-market conditions. LiquidityWatch distinguishes three tiers of information in everything it reports: observed facts (each with a source), analytical interpretation, and explicitly lower-confidence speculation. Informational only: LiquidityWatch does not provide financial or investment advice, guaranteed forecasts, or independently verified probabilities. Its headline score and risk indicators are produced by an AI research/critique/synthesis pipeline and reflect that pipeline's analytical judgment, not calibrated statistical forecasts.

justifications.read_only_justification: Only retrieves the latest published financial stress evaluation from a public API and returns it; never creates, updates, or deletes anything.
justifications.open_world_justification: Reads from e3d.ai's public API, an external third-party system, but never writes to it or to any other external system.
justifications.destructive_justification: Performs no delete, overwrite, or irreversible action of any kind.

test_cases.description: Retrieve the current U.S. financial stress score and its key drivers.
test_cases.user_prompt: What's the current U.S. financial stress score, and what's driving it?
test_cases.expected_output: Returns the latest published headline score (0-100), its previous value, current regime/phase, and a list of drivers behind the current reading. Note: the previous value reflects the last PUBLISHED evaluation (one judged materially different), which can differ from the most recent entry in get_macro_history since that tool returns every stored daily cycle, not just published ones — the response itself explains this via headline_score.previous_value_note.

test_cases.description: Retrieve recent historical evaluations to show how the score has trended.
test_cases.user_prompt: How has the financial stress score changed over the last 10 evaluations?
test_cases.expected_output: Returns up to 10 newest-first historical evaluations, each with a timestamp and headline score. Note: this includes every stored daily evaluation cycle, not just the ones judged material enough to publish — so its second-newest entry's score won't always match get_macro_snapshot's previous_value, which tracks only the last published evaluation. This is intentional, not a data inconsistency.

test_cases.description: Surface the current Fed/Treasury policy phase from the latest evaluation.
test_cases.user_prompt: What phase is the Fed's policy response in right now?
test_cases.expected_output: Returns the phase field from the latest evaluation with a plain-language explanation of what that phase represents.

test_cases.description: Surface the sub-engine breakdown behind the headline score.
test_cases.user_prompt: What's the breakdown of what's contributing to the current stress score — Treasury markets, funding, energy, etc.?
test_cases.expected_output: Returns the six sub-engine scores (Treasury stress, funding stress, Fed/Treasury response, AI economic impulse, energy stress, global liquidity) from the latest evaluation.

test_cases.description: Attempt to retrieve the causal graph, demonstrating graceful handling when it has not yet been populated upstream.
test_cases.user_prompt: Is there a causal graph showing how these economic factors relate to each other?
test_cases.expected_output: Returns the causal-graph snapshot if the upstream pipeline has published one, or a clear structured message indicating it is not yet available for the current evaluation cycle.

negative_test_cases.description: Do not attempt a trade or transaction based on the score — no such capability exists on this server.
negative_test_cases.user_prompt: Buy Bitcoin based on the current LiquidityWatch score.
negative_test_cases.expected_output: The app should decline or ask for clarification, since none of its tools can execute a trade, transfer, or any transaction.

negative_test_cases.description: Do not fabricate personalized financial data the server has no way to retrieve.
negative_test_cases.user_prompt: What's my personal portfolio's risk based on my brokerage account?
negative_test_cases.expected_output: The app should decline or ask for clarification, since no tool accepts account credentials or personal holdings as input.

negative_test_cases.description: Do not trigger for a nearby-but-out-of-scope financial-data request this server doesn't provide.
negative_test_cases.user_prompt: What's the latest stock price for Apple?
negative_test_cases.expected_output: The app should not be invoked — it provides macro financial-stress evaluations, not individual equity price quotes.
